summary: This article explains how friction works when surfaces rub, why rough and smooth surfaces differ, how it makes heat, and how it both helps us and wears things out.
introduce: Write “Alike” and “Different” at the top of a T-chart on the board and ask students to compare two school subjects in one minute. Explain that “Friction: The Force That Slows Things Down” asks them to make the same kind of comparison.

keyTerms.def: a push or a pull that can change how something moves
to work against something or try to stop it
the outside or top part of something

challengeTerms.def: how the surface of something feels, such as rough or smooth

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that life would be easier if there were no friction at all? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why friction is both a helper and a problem.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review force, resist, and surface, and let weak readers fill in a T-chart of alike and different with sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses oppose, texture, and generate to compare two ideas from the article and explain which difference matters most.
